pure-announcement.rationale: It is the normative Tools chapter of the MCP specification, not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: mcp-stateless-core already carries the explicit-handle state pattern and the input_required/requestState flow, but the rest of the tools surface — schema rules, naming, x-mcp-header, result content types, the two-tier error model, security requirements — is new to a reader of that concept.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is normative specification text, verifiable against the published 2026-07-28 MCP spec.

durability.rationale: It is pinned to the dated 2026-07-28 revision of a spec that has broken compatibility roughly every release, and its newest normative details (x-mcp-header, InputRequiredResult, subscriptions/listen) sit exactly where the protocol churns — only the core tools/list-tools/call model is stable.

actionability.rationale: An MCP server author acts on this directly: declare capabilities, keep tool ordering deterministic for prompt-cache hits, satisfy the schema rules, design handles for authorization/opacity/lifetime, and choose protocol errors versus isError results for model self-correction.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles several separable mechanisms — tool schema rules, header mirroring for body-blind routing, multi-round-trip input, handle-based state, the error split — that cohere as a reference chapter but do not reduce to one paragraph without losing most of the content.
